reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) strongly supports the first three premises regarding the alloy's behavior under slow and rapid cooling and the role of phosphorus. However, the last two premises—that a laser remelting treatment can achieve this and that the specific temperature window is effective—are not supported by the cited passages, which contain no mention of laser processing, localized remelting, or the proposed thermal window.
premises: Slow cooling produces a complex multiphase crystalline microstructure with primary non-eutectic phases (FCC, tetragonal, etc.)
Rapid cooling (10^5–10^6 K/s) yields a fully amorphous structure in this alloy
Phosphorus enhances glass-forming ability and promotes amorphization during rapid cooling
A laser pulse can locally remelt preformed crystals without fully melting the bulk, and subsequent ultrafast quenching can suppress re-nucleation
Applying this remelting treatment at ~1200–1297 K (just below full melting) will dissolve primary crystals and reset the microstructure to an amorphous state
